tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version. Leave it out to keep the current one.

Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. slug.description: The artifact's slug. Omit to create a new artifact.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
tools.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

schema.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
schema.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

base_version.description: Required when slug is given: the version id this publish replaces — echo the version get_artifact or read_artifact returned (or your last publish result's). Rejected with a conflict if it no longer names the live version, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten. Omit when creating.

content.description: The complete HTML document, at most 16 MiB. Must sniff as text/html — begin it with <!DOCTYPE html>.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Leave it out to keep the current one. Pass one only when the user asks for a different version, or this server's answer says to. If the publish is rejected because the contract is yanked or out of the supported window, republish with an explicit "0.0.0" to clear the contract — omitting the argument is not a reliable recovery (the server may carry the stored contract forward, repeating the rejection).

deadline.description: Optional, rarely needed: by when pages still open on an OLDER version must have moved to this one — one word: now, 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d, or an ISO-8601 time at most 30 days ahead. Omit it for ordinary edits (open pages then move at their next quiet moment); it cannot be relaxed once published.

favicon.description: Optional legacy emoji marker; omit it.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the artifact's tab icon — a plain signifier of what it is, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map; not a product or brand name. Pass one when creating; omit when republishing to keep the current icon.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

slug.description: The artifact's server-assigned slug (UUID), e.g. from list_artifacts, get_artifact or the artifact's own URL. Omit to create a new artifact.

title.description: Browser-tab title. Required when creating. When republishing it is optional — omitted, the new version keeps the current live version's title (the server also keeps the stored HTML's <title> element in sync with it); pass a value only to rename the artifact, never invent a new title on a routine republish.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__read_artifact
tools.description: Read the current document of an artifact: one that the user owns, or one that belongs to someone in the user's organization and that the user can open. Read a pasted claude.ai artifact link with this tool. Returns a JSON summary (slug, version id, title, favicon, runtime-contract version, total_lines, and for a multi-file artifact its file names), then the HTML of the version the user is served, then a reminder. The HTML, and the summary's title, favicon and file names, are wrapped in an <untrusted-document-...> tag that the summary's notice names; the tag is not part of them. A document over ~1 MiB is not served whole: read it in parts with offset and limit, which count lines; next_offset says where the next part starts. ## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|

| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |

| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|

If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

# Re-review rulings — 2026-10-27 (delegated: the user said "just use best judgment")

Marker for every edit that applies one of these: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling Rn)*.
In-text record where a decision is stated: "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling Rn (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): ..."
These rulings never reverse a prior user ruling; they settle consequences the user's rulings left ambiguous or unimplementable.

## General rules (G)
- G1 Owner wins: where two GDDs disagree on a value, field, unit or contract, the registry `source:` GDD wins and the other conforms. If the thing is unregistered, the PUBLISHER of the field/signal/value wins and the consumer conforms.
- G2 Specialist disagreements: follow the creative-director's stated resolution in that GDD's disagreements list. Where the CD said "the user should choose", take the CD's stated lean.
- G3 Carried-over blockers (flagged "still not fixed"/"carried over"): previous edits did not land. After each edit, Grep for the old wording and confirm it is gone everywhere in the GDD (body, examples, ACs, tuning tables, OQs).
- G4 ACs that contradict the GDD's own formulas: recompute from the formula at registry defaults; never weaken a formula to match an AC.
- G5 Division/overflow at boundaries: guard explicitly (e.g. avail == 0 -> share 0, everything unserved); state the guard in the formula and add a boundary AC.

## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. Update the kernel seq ACs (L883, L892, L902-904) and PC-7 together.
- R3 Completion sentinel (kernel CR-19b). Every owner callable receives `ctx`; results flow through ctx, never the return value: validate reports via ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason); snapshot via ctx.put(payload); apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx). Every callable's only return is `return ctx.complete()` (a typed token). No `-> void` owner callables.
- R4 Mouse aim. The Player Controller's form is canonical: cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre) / k_eff, where f_q is the quantized camera position actually used for the frame. The Pipeline PUBLISHES f_q. Aim direction = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN, with AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y) (ruling D10); remove the chest-based subtraction from the Pipeline's D.14b/D.7. Cursor units: the fixer must VERIFY the unit of the cursor source (e.g. Viewport.get_mouse_position() under the Pipeline's canvas_items stretch wiring (ii)) against docs/engine-reference/godot/ and the Pipeline's own wiring text, then make the label, the variable table and the divisor agree in both GDDs; if the reference cannot settle it, mark the unit claim [UNV] and add an in-engine verification AC.
- R5 Carry tell (consequence of X3). Owners: Attention owns the intake numbers and the ONE integrator (Attention's walk-in convention and tick accounting are canonical; Boarding quotes them); Boarding owns the live-choice acceptance (AC-BS-123) and its K definitions, stated with Attention's integrator; Derelict owns the route length (21-28 tiles, X3). Scope: the burden applies only to SALVAGE carry — an item carried that was picked up inside a non-home locus (derelict) — moving or standing, until dropped/installed/thrown; never to carrying at home or of the player's own kit. Pace-robustness, scoped to that salvage carry only: (a) while a salvage carry is held, attention decay is suspended (freezing with cargo is priced, per X3); (b) dropping and re-taking the same item grants no fresh TELL_REARM immunity (the rearm timer keys on the item, not the pickup). Attention may re-derive weights/theta within these scoped rules, but must NOT invent weights to force K3-K5 green: all values stay PLACEHOLDER, and if the live-choice margin cannot be shown on paper with honest numbers, AC-BS-123(d) is re-written as a spike gate (owner, the boarding spike, its pass line), which is the expected outcome.
- R6 Pod statuses (consequence of user ruling D60 "statuses run in the pod"). Suit's reading stands: the reserve drains, the cell drains while lit, source RESERVE. Web Map conforms: delete WM-17b's HOLD reading and close ASK-S2. Pillar-2 mitigation: the valve click plays only on the source TRANSITION edge (once when breath_src becomes RESERVE), never per run. Recompute every pod-leg figure from the registry's own leg formula at registry defaults (ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS default 45, not 180; the registry's formulas use 945 ticks per leg — verify in the registry before using) and state run counts with an explicit floor and a carried remainder so every "exactly N" oracle is an integer.
- R7 PD1 static spill bound (user ruling D31: 'static authored spill <= 24 px'). The bound stays 24 px — it is the user's number. The home ship's spine_corridor (computed 26 px) must be brought within it by Derelict Authoring (light placement, fixture position or corridor dressing — the least invasive change; show the recomputed s <= 24). Lighting's AC-LO-69 stays per-push BLOCKING.
- R8 Units of a request field shared by producer and consumer (e.g. Perception LEVEL vs Audio): G1 — the producer defines the unit; the consumer converts. State the unit in both GDDs with the conversion.
- R9 Undesigned dependencies (VS/Alpha systems with no GDD): not a blocker; keep them listed as "undesigned — provisional contract" with the interface this GDD assumes.
- R10 Pending-confirmation defaults and PLACEHOLDER values are not changed by these rulings unless a blocker shows them internally inconsistent.
- R11 X14 (reference machine) stays OPEN: never name or invent a reference machine, build type or spec anywhere.

Determinism.** *Rule.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* The two draw kernels (Attention's `restore_epoch` key and a Horror-private epoch seed) are replaced by the one below; Attention's AT-8 calls the same function. All simulation randomness is `rng_derive(world_seed, "horror.tell", counter_eff)`, used for the REACH length only, where `counter_eff = threat_counter(counter)` and **`threat_counter(c) = c + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch` is the kernel's one derivation for threat draws** (the stream-name hash stays cached and unchanged; Attention and Horror call it and neither defines its own). `restore_epoch` is a persisted unsigned integer in the save slot header, **owned by Save/Load** (u32, starts at 0): on every restore, whether a death restart or a load, in-process or after a fresh process start, Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (an atomic header-only write) **before the first RUNNING tick**, so reloading the same autosave twice gives a new epoch each time and quit-and-continue is no reroll oracle. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)`, sim-visible and pure. `RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` is 1,048,576 (2^20) and is the kernel's constant (registry request: its source moves from Attention to the kernel, with Attention, Horror and Save/Load in `referenced_by`); the lint `counter < RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` holds. Horror reads `restore_epoch` through `threat_counter` at the draw and at no other time, never stores it in `horror.state` and never decides when it advances; the Graph's physical failures and every persisted counter never read it. The persisted `"horror.tell"` counter is restored exactly, so no draw is reused at one epoch and the counter never moves backwards, and a REACH already in flight keeps its stored length (`reach_end_T`, E-HE-36). **Determinism (G4) is defined given the pair (save bytes, `restore_epoch`)**: the same pair replays identically (strike lengths, positions, marks, `state_hash`), tests pin the epoch, and a restore that advances the epoch changes only the lengths of REACHes not yet begun. Nothing physical is re-keyed: mark seeds, LURK waypoint choice and L3 timing are pure integer hashes of ids, the run index and `HE_HASH_SEED` through `he_hash` (below), so the trail and the positions the player can read in the world replay exactly (Pillar 1); they are not threat draws, since the REACH length is Horror's only draw. No wall clock and no global RNG (H9). **`he_hash`** *(defined 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier text said "pure integer hash" with no function or sign rule)*: `he_hash(k1, k2, k3, salt) = lsr(mix64( mix64(k1 ⊕ HE_HASH_SEED) ⊕ mix64(k2 ⊕ salt) ⊕ (k3 × GOLDEN) ), 1)`, on the kernel's pinned `mix64`, `lsr` and `GOLDEN` (kernel D.10) with the intended wrap on the multiplication; the final logical shift makes the result non-negative (63 bits), so every `mod` in this GDD acts on a non-negative integer and no reduction depends on a sign convention. `HE_HASH_SEED` defaults to `0x4845` (any fixed integer; changing it re-rolls every mark seed, LURK waypoint and L3 timing). The salts are fixed constants: `SALT_MARK` 1, `SALT_WP` 2, `SALT_L3_START` 3, `SALT_L3_STRENGTH` 4, `SALT_L3_DUR` 5. Callers: mark seed `he_hash(mark_id, 0, 0, SALT_MARK)`; waypoint rank `he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP)`; L3 `h1`, `h2`, `h3` = `he_hash(emitter_id, run_n, 0, SALT_L3_START)`, `…SALT_L3_STRENGTH)`, `…SALT_L3_DUR)`. Golden vectors are pinned by AC-HE-139. -> ADR candidate (4): a shared pure-integer presentation hash with Lighting LO-19. *Cites.* KRN D.10, D.12, H9.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

All simulation randomness is `rng_derive(world_seed, "horror.tell", counter_eff)`, used for the REACH length only, where `counter_eff = threat_counter(counter)` and **`threat_counter(c) = c + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch` is the kernel's one derivation for threat draws** (the stream-name hash stays cached and unchanged; Attention and Horror call it and neither defines its own). `restore_epoch` is a persisted unsigned integer in the save slot header, **owned by Save/Load** (u32, starts at 0): on every restore, whether a death restart or a load, in-process or after a fresh process start, Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (an atomic header-only write) **before the first RUNNING tick**, so reloading the same autosave twice gives a new epoch each time and quit-and-continue is no reroll oracle. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)`, sim-visible and pure. `RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` is 1,048,576 (2^20) and is the kernel's constant (registry request: its source moves from Attention to the kernel, with Attention, Horror and Save/Load in `referenced_by`); the lint `counter < RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` holds. Horror reads `restore_epoch` through `threat_counter` at the draw and at no other time, never stores it in `horror.state` and never decides when it advances; the Graph's physical failures and every persisted counter never read it. The persisted `"horror.tell"` counter is restored exactly, so no draw is reused at one epoch and the counter never moves backwards, and a REACH already in flight keeps its stored length (`reach_end_T`, E-HE-36). **Determinism (G4) is defined given the pair (save bytes, `restore_epoch`)**: the same pair replays identically (strike lengths, positions, marks, `state_hash`), tests pin the epoch, and a restore that advances the epoch changes only the lengths of REACHes not yet begun. Nothing physical is re-keyed: mark seeds, LURK waypoint choice and L3 timing are pure integer hashes of ids, the run index and `HE_HASH_SEED` through `he_hash` (below), so the trail and the positions the player can read in the world replay exactly (Pillar 1); they are not threat draws, since the REACH length is Horror's only draw. No wall clock and no global RNG (H9). **`he_hash`** *(defined 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier text said "pure integer hash" with no function or sign rule)*: `he_hash(k1, k2, k3, salt) = lsr(mix64( mix64(k1 ⊕ HE_HASH_SEED) ⊕ mix64(k2 ⊕ salt) ⊕ (k3 × GOLDEN) ), 1)`, on the kernel's pinned `mix64`, `lsr` and `GOLDEN` (kernel D.10) with the intended wrap on the multiplication; the final logical shift makes the result non-negative (63 bits), so every `mod` in this GDD acts on a non-negative integer and no reduction depends on a sign convention. `HE_HASH_SEED` defaults to `0x4845` (any fixed integer; changing it re-rolls every mark seed, LURK waypoint and L3 timing). The salts are fixed constants: `SALT_MARK` 1, `SALT_WP` 2, `SALT_L3_START` 3, `SALT_L3_STRENGTH` 4, `SALT_L3_DUR` 5. Callers: mark seed `he_hash(mark_id, 0, 0, SALT_MARK)`; waypoint rank `he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP)`; L3 `h1`, `h2`, `h3` = `he_hash(emitter_id, run_n, 0, SALT_L3_START)`, `…SALT_L3_STRENGTH)`, `…SALT_L3_DUR)`. # Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`

input.old_string: `restore_epoch` is a persisted unsigned integer in the save slot header, **owned by Save/Load** (u32, starts at 0): on every restore, whether a death restart or a load, in-process or after a fresh process start, Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (an atomic header-only write) **before the first RUNNING tick**, so reloading the same autosave twice gives a new epoch each time and quit-and-continue is no reroll oracle.
input.new_string: `restore_epoch` is a persisted u32 **owned by Save/Load** (starts at 0), held in the per-slot side file `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32, written atomically by temp file and rename by the Save/Load worker); it is in no generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA never change, and each generation header carries only a read-only copy for recovery (R14). A death-stub restore advances it by 1; a Continue of a `QUIT` generation that is the newest non-demoted verified generation carries it unchanged (R13, user ruling D16: not steerable by quit); a Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback), in-process or after a fresh process start, advances it. Save/Load writes an advance in a pre-restore staging step and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`; on a failed write or after `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder) it proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (a listed exposure: a kill before a later successful write may replay that epoch once). So two death restores of one autosave give two new epochs, and a Save & Quit then Continue replays the same REACH lengths: quit-and-continue is no reroll oracle *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14; cross-GDD fix)*.

content.content: 186	**HE-19. Strike scope is geometry, not intent.** *Rule.* Resolution reads only Layout `room_at`, `room_adjacency` (open or closed leaf), `door_passage`, the horror's and the seats' integer positions, and `solid_in` for the horror's own movement. No `probe()` and no physics query. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **The one Layout read Horror still requires, `door_passage(section_id, via_id)`.** `room_adjacency` names a DOOR or HATCH record (`via_id`) but publishes no geometry and no openness for it, so the REACH, standoff and pathing rules cite one further read, specified here as Horror's required contract: `door_passage(section_id, via_id) -> {orientation EW|NS, sill_rect, gap_rect, open_extent_px, passable_f_px}`, pure and integer, section-local base px. `sill_rect` is the door cell rectangle; `gap_rect` is the open, **hinge-aware** part of it (for a partially open leaf the gap lies on the side away from the hinge, so it is not centred on the sill); `open_extent_px` is the open width along the wall run (0 when closed); `passable_f_px` is the free width the foot box would have across the run, and the leaf is *passable* iff `passable_f_px >= foot_extent(orientation)`, where `foot_extent` is `FOOT_BOX_W` 16 across an E-W wall run and `FOOT_BOX_H` 8 across a N-S wall run (the foot box is 16 wide and 8 deep, so a single 16 px threshold is wrong for one of the two orientations). **Layout has not published this read** (Open Question 32); there is no `solid_in` sampling fallback, because the five `solid_in` queries per run (HE-43) already belong to movement. Until it is published, AC-HE-127 and AC-HE-128 read NOT ASSESSED against a stub and never PASS, and the slice-2 stories (Open Question 29) do not start on a stub. **Two room predicates, split on purpose.** (1) `linked(a, b)`, for every Horror *movement* distance rule: true iff `room_hops(room_at(a), room_at(b)) <= LINK_ROOM_HOPS` (default 2, range 1 to 3) over the room graph whose edges are the DOOR and HATCH records of `room_adjacency` with `open_extent_px > 0` (open at all, whatever the width). It depends only on the two room ids and the open or closed state of the doors, so it is constant while both stand in their rooms: a horror at a doorway cannot flip between the standoff and the step-away rule from a one-pixel move, and a seat two short rooms away in open line of sight is linked; a door opening or closing flips it as one discrete event. (2) `connected(a, b)`, for REACH begin only (HE-14 (f)): true iff `room_at(a) == room_at(b)`, or the two rooms are adjacent through a DOOR or HATCH record whose leaf is *passable* and the straight integer segment `a → b` crosses that record's `gap_rect` (an integer segment-against-axis-aligned-rectangle test; no ray, no float, no physics query). The strike's wall test (HE-15) is stricter than both, **strictly the same room**, so the second branch of `connected` never reaches a seat. `linked` is the test for the `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` standoff and step-away tests of HE-11, HE-12 and HE-17, the waypoint filter of HE-11, and the standoff clause of the ingress legality test of HE-20 and HE-F9; `connected` is the test for REACH condition (f) and for the anchor REACH. A door waypoint (HE-25) is the centre of `gap_rect`. The straight segment from the horror's foot point to P must not cross a closed door leaf (checked through the room-graph sill, not a ray). The same-room test (HE-15) is re-evaluated at resolution against the *current* layout, so a weld or cut during a REACH is honoured while the locked point stays the stored integer it was.

content.thinking: I want to simplify the explanation so it just states the segment test once: the straight integer segment from a to b crosses gap_rect if and only if it intersects the closed occupied span, using an integer cross-multiplication test rather than floating point.

input.old_string: **The one Layout read Horror still requires, `door_passage(section_id, via_id)`.** `room_adjacency` names a DOOR or HATCH record (`via_id`) but publishes no geometry and no openness for it, so the REACH, standoff and pathing rules cite one further read, specified here as Horror's required contract: `door_passage(section_id, via_id) -> {orientation EW|NS, sill_rect, gap_rect, open_extent_px, passable_f_px}`, pure and integer, section-local base px. `sill_rect` is the door cell rectangle; `gap_rect` is the open, **hinge-aware** part of it (for a partially open leaf the gap lies on the side away from the hinge, so it is not centred on the sill); `open_extent_px` is the open width along the wall run (0 when closed); `passable_f_px` is the free width the foot box would have across the run, and the leaf is *passable* iff `passable_f_px >= foot_extent(orientation)`, where `foot_extent` is `FOOT_BOX_W` 16 across an E-W wall run and `FOOT_BOX_H` 8 across a N-S wall run (the foot box is 16 wide and 8 deep, so a single 16 px threshold is wrong for one of the two orientations). **Layout has not published this read** (Open Question 32); there is no `solid_in` sampling fallback, because the five `solid_in` queries per run (HE-43) already belong to movement. Until it is published, AC-HE-127 and AC-HE-128 read NOT ASSESSED against a stub and never PASS, and the slice-2 stories (Open Question 29) do not start on a stub.
input.new_string: **The Layout read for door geometry, `door_passage(section_id, via_id)`** (published: Layout LY-28 and D.5, AC-180) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. `via_id` is the `room_adjacency` record's `via_id` (Layout's `door_index`). It returns `{orientation EW|NS, sill_rect, gap_rect, open_extent_px}`: pure, integer, section-local base px; rects are Layout's OUT convention, the occupied span (x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1); `sill_rect` is the door cell rectangle; `gap_rect` is NONE when `open_extent_px` is 0. Data path: the Graph's `opening(edge_id) = {area, area_max, door_state}` → Layout's `layout.doors` (P3, runs before `body.integrate`, which runs before `horror.step`, so a run sees same-tick state) → `open_extent_px = floor_div(96 × area, area_max)`; Horror never calls `opening()` and owns no door state. `gap_rect` is **hinge-aware** (for a partially open leaf the open part lies on the side away from the hinge, so it is not centred on the sill). A leaf is *passable* iff `open_extent_px >= foot_extent(orientation)`, with `foot_extent` = `FOOT_BOX_W` 16 across an E-W wall run and `FOOT_BOX_H` 8 across a N-S wall run (Body's foot box, cited; Layout's `passes(F)`; the foot box is 16 wide and 8 deep, so a single 16 px threshold is wrong for one of the two orientations). The result changes only when `version(section_id)` changes, so HE-25's cache key is unchanged. There is no `solid_in` sampling fallback, because the five `solid_in` queries per run (HE-43) already belong to movement. **The segment test, stated once:** the straight integer segment a → b crosses `gap_rect` iff it meets the closed occupied span [x0, x1−1] × [y0, y1−1] (integer cross-multiplication; no ray, no float, no physics query).

The bound above carries the `+ 1` on top of that count as a deliberate margin, so under this convention the exact slack at `U` = 95 is 4 ticks (5 cardinal), and the 3 (4) quoted in this document is the conservative figure that also spends the margin; AC-HE-130 pins the real kernel order, and a kernel change that applied commands later than `T + 1` would consume the margin first. `rng_int` is drawn from `rng_derive(world_seed, "horror.tell", threat_counter(counter))`, where `threat_counter(c) = c + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch` is the kernel's one restore-epoch derivation (kernel D.10; HE-42; user ruling X8/D16) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)*; the stream is Horror's REACH length only and is **not** a tell length (HE-9). The scale is applied after the draw in integer order, `UNFOLD_TICKS = 5 × ceil_div(draw × UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT, 100)` (draw 21 at scale 105: `ceil_div(2205, 100) = 23`, so 115); the rounding order is fixed, so there is no sign or rounding ambiguity *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.

content.content:
**HE-22. Weld and cut.** *Rule.* The path cache is keyed by the layout (HE-25) and recomputed on any `layout.state` change (a weld or cut applying, MSA-14 / MSA-20). If a weld changes `locus_body` membership, the target body is re-derived from `locus_section_id` on the next run (`locus_body` is recorded at TELL entry and is replaced mid-epoch only by an AT-14 fallback, which TellAudit records as LOCUS_FALLBACK; Horror re-reads `locus_section_id` each run). If a cut removes the section the record stands in from its body, the record's `body_id` is re-derived from `body_of(section_id)`; if its section is gone the record goes to TRANSIT with an egress mark and re-enters its home body. Horror has no cut verb and does not interrupt a cut; Modular Ship Assembly states the same ("Horror and Attention have no cut verb; the breach rhythm uses STRESS and M17, not detaches", MSA-22). *Cites.* MSA-14 / MSA-20 (weld and cut apply), MSA-22 (no cut verb).
----
**HE-34. Emitter subjects.** *Rule.* Each non-TRANSIT record is an Emitter HORROR subject: E6 `register_subject(ref, HORROR, anchor_px, section_id)` at arrival, E8 `set_subject_anchor(ref, anchor_px)` once per run (E8 is called once per run and lands at the next `emitter.place`: the one-tick lag EM:154 accepts. The anchor is otherwise current, because the sim position changes only at runs (HE-23)), E7 `unregister_subject(ref)` at egress or unload; registrations are canonical in `emitter.state` and survive a restore (EM-28, EM:712); in its own `post_restore` the record calls E6 only when it is non-TRANSIT and its ref is absent from the Emitter subject table; a duplicate E6 returns false by design (EM:152) and is not a defect. HORROR is always `moving` (EM-21). An unregistered ref answers like an unlit one (`lux` 0, `lit` false). A false return from E6 on a first registration (the `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` overflow, `emitter_subjects_overflow` increments, EM AC-27) is a **budget defect** (the subject reads dark) and a lint or acceptance-criterion failure, never a gameplay state; a false return on an already-registered ref is not. Horror reads `lux(ref)` only (its lit test is the stateless `lux_pm >= LIT_ON_PM` of HE-13, not the Emitter's `lit` bit) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; it calls no `probe` at MVP (Emitter EM-24 anticipates Horror pathing probes; HE-25 pathing needs none, so Horror consumes none of `MAX_PROBES_PER_TICK` 4, shared with Interaction (Attention makes no `probe()` call and does not read it, AT-4), and "Horror spams probes: only `probes_allowed` are served", EM:723). `HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 (one active plus one transient during ingress), range 1 to 12; the Emitter's "placeholder 12" (EM:229) is a ceiling Horror owns, not the plan; I-CAPS (d) holds (2 + actors 4 ≤ `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS` 16). Interaction's `H` (REG `subject_budget`) and Derelict Authoring's `HORRORS` now quote this registered number, `HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 (C-HE-4, closed 2026-10-27). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **One registration rule, for body load and `post_restore` alike:** a record is an Emitter subject iff it is non-TRANSIT and its body is loaded. On every run, after guard 2 and before guard 3, the record reconciles: body loaded, non-TRANSIT and its ref absent from the Emitter subject table, then E6 at its stored `pos_px` (this is the first run after a body loads, including first boarding, and the first run after a restore, so a resident LURK in derelict B reads lit the moment the player boards, which the CALM-sighting goal needs); body unloaded and the ref still registered, then E7 once. Both calls are idempotent through the table read, and neither is a step: an unloaded record performs no other act (HE-21). AC-HE-140. *Cites.* EM-21, EM-24, EM:229.
----
- **AC-HE-48 (auto) Weld and cut.** GIVEN a weld mid-path and a cut removing the record's section, WHEN the next run executes, THEN the path cache is recomputed, `body_id` is re-derived from `body_of`, a record with no section goes TRANSIT with an egress mark, and `locus_body` is unchanged by the weld (only an AT-14 fallback, recorded as LOCUS_FALLBACK, replaces it mid-epoch). *Covers HE-22, E-HE-29, E-HE-30.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Modular Ship Assembly is `Status: Designed`; testable.)*
-----
- **AC-HE-76 (auto) Block conformance.** GIVEN `horror.state`, WHEN conformance tests run, THEN class SIM, `persist` true, `persist_scope` WORLD, scope SHARED, `repl_hint` SHARED_SUMMARY, `schema_version` 1, `supported_versions` [1], `restore_after` `[layout.state, graph.state, emitter.state, attention.state]`; plain data only (no `StringName` keys, no `Vector2i` values); **the snapshot's key set equals the committed manifest** `tests/unit/horror_entities/horror_state_manifest.json` (one row per HE-41 field: name, type, range, group; no key beyond the manifest and none missing), which is reviewed against the HE-41 text and never generated from the implementation; **a mutation test**: for each manifest field a fixture snapshot is perturbed to a different in-range value, restored and run for 600 ticks from a fixture in which that field is read, and the run's `state_hash` must differ from the unperturbed continuation (a field that changes nothing is dead state and a defect; the fixture per field is part of the manifest); **a lint** of the `horror.step` source finds no instance field that is read in a later run, is not in the manifest and is not on the non-persisted whitelist (the target, the path cache, `horror.view.debug`); the snapshot contains neither the target nor the path cache; `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is byte-identical; the ring never exceeds `MAX_MARKS` 32 and no quota'd kind exceeds its quota; `gouged_seg_ids` never exceeds `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX`. *Covers HE-41, E-HE-46.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier row checked "every field of HE-41 is present", which tested the implementation against its own list and let the gaps pass review twice)*
